adjudication.rationale: In `Office365CalendarService.createEvent`, the URL is built from the first destination calendar only: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then `eventsUrl = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events` : ...` (Office365CalendarService.ts). Meanwhile, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now supports multiple destination calendars and creates events per host/destination, selecting the host credential per `destination.credentialId` and calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. However, `CalendarManager.createEvent` passes only `(calEvent, credential.id)` to `calendar.createEvent`, and Office365’s implementation does not use `credential.id` (nor any externalId) to choose the matching destination calendar; it always uses index 0. So for multi-host collective bookings where destinationCalendar[0] belongs to a different host than the current credential token, Office365 will attempt `/me/calendars/{firstHostExternalId}/events` with another host’s token, plausibly causing 404 and preventing those hosts’ calendars from receiving the event.
